scenes.text: Claude built it in four phases, one prompt each. Every day has a morning and an afternoon, so Christmas Eve to the twenty-eighth costs two days, not five. Holidays and weekends are never charged.
But the useful part is what broke. Just viewing last year created allowance rows, which then blocked closing the current year. And the calendar didn't say whether a holiday or a day off wins.
Honestly, Timetastic is cheap. A dollar fifty per user per month. Build it when you want your own leave rules and data, next to your other internal tools.
